reason: A is basically the original shrunk and stacked down the centre. The body copy is too small to read at 300x250, the headline is undersized for the format, the CTA is tiny, and the oversized peach and green circles crowd the text, with the subhead running across the edge of the peach circle. B actually rearranges the layout: the logo sits left, the can moves right inside the green circle, and the headline is large and full-width, which gives clear hierarchy. Its flaws: the bottom row is cramped, with the body copy jammed into the corner on top of the peach circle and the CTA close to the right edge, and the SOLSTICE wordmark floats in empty space with weak alignment.

A keeps the original reading order and hierarchy, and the headline rewraps sensibly to 4 lines. However, the dark brand header is a band that stops short of both side edges instead of spanning the full width. The vertical stack is also tightly packed: the legal text sits jammed against the bottom edge and there is very little space between the CTA and the copy around it. B breaks the design apart: the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow drops to the bottom-left, below the headline, and the orange divider is left on its own under the logo block. The CTA is tiny and loses prominence, 'Ships late June' sits apart from its button, and the legal text is crushed into an unreadable narrow column. The 7-line headline is too heavy for the space and squeezes everything else.

A: The dark header has turned into a partial block in the top-left, and the headline is pushed right up under it. The orange divider is stranded alone at the far-right edge, and the body copy, 'Ships late June' and the legal line are tiny and hard to read, so a lot of the canvas is dead space. B: The dark bar is left as an empty floating rectangle, cut off from the logo, which now sits on the cream background. The divider floats between the two columns, and the headline, body copy and button crowd the canvas edges. Even so, its text is much larger and more readable and the two-column banner reads more clearly, so it is the less bad of the two.

A is a shrunk copy of the original. The SOLSTICE logo and the '25% off' line are microscopic, the CTA label is barely readable, the headline leaves 'last' orphaned on its own line, and there is dead space above the logo and between the CTA and the legal text. B makes good use of the tall format and its headline and CTA are clearly legible, but the headline breaks into one word per line (the word 'the' sits alone), the tiny logo is pushed against the top edge, the ribbon crowds the phone, and the bottom stack of offer line, CTA and legal text is cramped against the bottom edge.

A: the body copy sits on top of the pale circle and is jammed against the left edge, the can is pulled away from its circle, SOLSTICE now sits below the headline, and the CTA and badge pills butt against each other in a cramped row. Still, the headline clearly dominates. B is more fragmented: SOLSTICE touches the left edge, the circle and can are separated, and the headline is tiny with 'back' orphaned on its own line. The badges float alone along the bottom, and the CTA is stranded far right, so nothing reads as a group.

A keeps the original's centred stack and hierarchy, but the headline is jammed near the top edge and wraps awkwardly as 'and a / little sunshine', which strands 'and a' at the end of line one. The vertical rhythm is also tight. B blows the headline up until it nearly touches the side edges, then pushes the subhead (now wrapped into two lines) and the CTA into a cramped bottom-right row that sits close to the headline and the canvas corner. The centred headline over that off-axis cluster mixes alignment axes and looks crowded rather than deliberate.

A keeps one clean left edge at x≈74 for the wordmark, headline, subline and chips. Its flaws: the CTA is wedged between the subline and the chips, and its right edge (~698) doesn't match the headline's (~724). The peach circle shrinks to a token corner blob, and the bottom band is mostly empty. B breaks the grid: the text starts at x≈26 but the chips start at x≈74, and the chips are spaced to their own centred rhythm. The oversized CTA is pushed almost onto the right edge (~742), and the chips hang under it as a disconnected row.

A keeps the cream circle with the product and the pill buttons, but the circle is jammed into the top-left corner, touching the canvas edges. The subtitle is indented off the headline's left edge, and the right-aligned NEW and Try It stack doesn't line up with the text column. B breaks badly: the cream circle has come loose from the can and sits on top of the 'S' of 'Sunset', so the can almost disappears against the orange background. B's rounded pill buttons have turned into rectangles, and NEW and Try It are staggered at random.

A changes the headline and subline from white to a dark maroon/brown that has poor contrast on the orange (an off-brand colour change), and the product circle is cropped at the left canvas edge. B keeps the white headline and the whole can badge, so it is more faithful to the original. Both have a subline that is too small to read at 320x50, NEW/Try It pills that are tiny and cramped, and a wide empty gap between the copy and the buttons.

A is broken: the cream circle has been pulled away from the bottle and now sits behind the 'B' of the headline, which is an obvious collision. The bottle loses its badge backdrop, the pill buttons have turned into square-cornered rectangles (off brand), and the NEW and Try It buttons sit on unrelated, ragged x-positions, leaving dead space top-right. B keeps the bottle-in-circle badge, the rounded pill buttons and a clear top-down order. The pills share a right edge, but the headline is left-aligned, so the two blocks don't line up. B's flaws: the bottle cap touches the top edge and sticks out of its circle, a stray faint circle sits in the corner, and the bottom-left is left empty.

A keeps the bottle inside its cream circle, the pill buttons and a clean left-aligned headline. However, everything is packed into the top 60% of the canvas, leaving a large empty orange area at the bottom. The NEW/Try It stack is pushed right, away from the headline's left edge, and the decorative circle is cropped awkwardly in the corner. B has lost the bottle's cream circle, which is now a stray blob colliding with the 'Blood'/'Sunset' headline on the left edge. The headline nearly runs edge to edge, the buttons have lost their pill shape (square corners), and the centred NEW chip and right-hugging Try It button don't share an axis.

I'd pick A because it at least keeps a readable headline. 'Sunset Sessions' and 'Saturday 21 June' are legible and lead left to right. Its flaws: the description and venue copy is crammed into illegible micro-text on the right, the pills are jammed against the top edge, the logo is gone, and the RSVP CTA is shrunk to a tiny buried line. B has a clear CTA button on the right, but the headline, date, venue, description and pill labels are all too small to read at banner size. It is spread into four weak, scattered columns with no focal point, so it reads like a shrunk copy of the original rather than a rearranged one.

A: the two-line quote is barely legible at 320x50, and the bold yellow attribution is as loud as the quote, which flattens the hierarchy. The quote mark is crammed into the top-left corner, the attribution sits below and to the left of the quote with no shared edge, the product is shrunk to an unreadable sliver on the right, and the Solstice logo is missing. B: the quote is squeezed onto one line at microscopic size and the letter-spaced attribution is illegible. The quote mark is a speck against the left edge, the product and circles are crushed into the bottom-right corner, the logo is lost and most of the banner is empty, so it reads even worse than A.

A has a clear top-to-bottom order and a strong headline, but the logo is blown up into a huge circle that competes with the product. The coffee bag is shrunk to a small thumbnail, and the CTA sits too close to the bottom edge. B is broken: the blurred background has split from the bag and left an empty brown square. The bag sits low and runs off the bottom, the headline is undersized, the body copy leaves 'like.' alone on its own line, and the top cluster is jammed against the left edge.

A has no collisions and keeps a clear logo, headline, product, copy order. However, the shoe-in-circle is shrunk into the bottom-left so the product looks minor. 'Full review inside' floats loosely to its right on no shared grid, the NEW VIDEO badge sits off the logo's line, and there is dead space below the headline. B is broken: the white headline runs onto the lime circle, so 'on' and 'ons' become low-contrast white-on-lime. The shoe has come off its circle and is blown up past it, which breaks the original's contained product badge, and the bottom-left caption is cramped against the shoe.

A breaks the key image apart: the shoe is pulled off its lime circle, leaving the circle empty on the right. The NEW VIDEO pill is clipped at the canvas edge, the VOLTSTRIDE logo is too small to read, the headline is small, and there is a large empty band in the middle. B keeps the brand and gives the one-line headline strong, clear prominence. However, 'Full review inside.' is stacked on top of the lime circle and shoe, an unwanted text collision. The shoe is also squeezed small inside the circle, and the NEW VIDEO pill is crammed under the logo at a tiny size.

A: the card is too narrow, so the headline 'The Reading Marathon' and the body copy run past both sides of the card onto the busy confetti. The lantern logo also pokes out above the card's top edge. These are clear collisions, with text sitting on a busy image. B: all text stays inside the card and the headline dominates, but the Inkwell & Lantern logo is shrunk to an illegible speck in the top-left corner. The fine print is tiny and squeezed in beside the CTA, the body/CTA/legal row is awkwardly split, and dead space is left at the bottom of the card.

A is just the original portrait layout shrunk into a tiny island in the middle of the banner. Every piece of text, the cards and the CTA are unreadable specks surrounded by empty grey, so it is unusable. B properly reflows the design for a banner: logo, plan cards, a large headline and a prominent orange CTA. Its flaws are that the subtitle under the logo, the card labels and the legal line under the headline are illegibly small, the card order is changed (6, 80, 48), so the dark Yearly card moves from the centre to the end, and the left cluster is cramped.

A actually rearranges the layout for the banner: the logo sits on the left, the can sits on the green circle on the right, and a large headline leads the hierarchy. However, the headline nearly touches both side edges, the bottom row (body copy and CTA) is pressed against the bottom edge, and the body copy sits half on the yellow circle. B is just a shrunken copy of the original. Its body line is tiny and hard to read, and it runs across the edge of the yellow circle. The CTA label is minuscule, the headline is too small to dominate, and the large yellow circle crowds the lower-left text block.

A scatters the layout. The 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow sits orphaned at the bottom left under the logo panel, below the headline it introduces. The orange divider floats alone under the dark block. The body copy, the shrunken 'Reserve a Case' button, 'Ships late June' and a narrow column of illegible legal text are jammed into one cramped bottom row, so the reading order and hierarchy fall apart. B keeps the original's vertical order and hierarchy, and its reflowed headline is well proportioned. However, the dark header band stops short of both edges, so it looks like a clipped box rather than a full-width bar. The vertical spacing is tight, with the legal line crowding the bottom edge, and the fine print is barely readable.

A: the dark header band survives only as a stray black slab at the top centre, cut away from the logo, and the orange divider floats between the columns. The body copy is jammed against the top edge and the headline nearly touches the left edge. Even so, the headline, body, CTA and legal line are all readable, and the CTA is strong. B: the dark block sits as an awkward top-left chunk that crowds the headline. Body copy, CTA and 'Ships late June' are tiny, the legal line is illegible, the divider is stranded at the far right and the right third of the canvas is empty.

A uses the skyscraper well with a large stacked headline and a clear CTA, but it is cramped. The logo is tiny, the sale banner is jammed under it, the legal text is almost as big as the subhead and sits against the bottom edge, and the CTA has no room around it. B shrinks everything: the headline is small with 'last' left alone on its own line, and the logo, subhead, CTA label and legal text are too small to read at this size. It also leaves big dead areas, and the sale ribbon nearly touches both side edges.

A: the headline is tiny, barely bigger than the body copy, and wraps with 'back' left alone on its own line. The SOLSTICE wordmark runs over the edge of the circle, and the can is pulled off the circle. The badges hang below the row, the CTA is pushed against the right edge, and wide dead gaps leave no clear hierarchy. B: the headline is large and clearly dominant, but the wordmark sits below it, so the reading order is reversed. The body copy is jammed against the left edge on top of the circle, the can is separated from the circle, and the CTA is crammed into the badge row at the same size as the badges. B is still the less broken of the two.

A: the oversized headline nearly hits the left and right edges (about 30px margins). The centred headline sits over a subcopy+CTA row pushed to the right, so there is no shared axis and the bottom-left is empty. The subcopy is also cramped right under the descenders. B: keeps the original's centred stack and hierarchy, but the headline breaks awkwardly after 'and a', the vertical spacing is tight, and the CTA sits only about 22px from the bottom edge.

A: the flavour chips are centred and spread out, starting at x≈73 while all the text starts at x≈26, so they don't share the text's left edge. The headline sits tight to the left edge, and the oversized CTA is wedged right under the subtitle and crowds the chips. B keeps one left edge (x≈73) for the wordmark, headline, subtitle and chips, which makes it clearly more intentional. Its flaws: the CTA is squeezed between the subtitle and the chips with almost no gap and doesn't line up with the headline's right end, the headline nearly touches the right edge, and the bottom quarter is empty except for a small leftover peach circle.

A: the cream circle has come away from the can and now sits behind the 'S' of 'Sunset', an obvious collision. The can floats on the orange with no backing, so it washes out. Both buttons have lost their pill shape, and NEW and Try It are staggered on different axes. B: the can stays on its cream circle, the buttons keep their pill shape, and the headline is clear. But the circle is pushed against the top and left edges of the canvas, the subhead is indented and doesn't line up with the headline's left edge, and the right-aligned buttons sit on a different axis from the left-aligned text, leaving the lower left empty.

Both are straight proportional shrinks of the leaderboard into 320x50 with no reflow. The subline 'New botanical sparkling, out now.' is about 6–7 px in both, which is unreadable on a phone. A keeps a legible serif headline, and its NEW pill and 'Try It' button are slightly larger, so the CTA is more readable. B's subline has collapsed letter spacing ('Newbotanical'), and its 'Try It' label is tiny inside a small button, so the CTA gets lost and the type looks broken.

A keeps the bottle in its cream circle and has a strong headline. Its flaws are a stray faint circle clipped at the top-left corner, NEW and Try It pills of different widths that only share a right edge, and a large empty lower-left area. B separates the cream circle from the bottle and drops it behind the 'B' of the headline, which is a clear unwanted collision. B also turns the pill buttons into squared rectangles, losing the brand shape, and staggers NEW and Try It so they share no edge or axis.

A broke the bottle-in-cream-circle badge apart: the stray cream circle now sits under the 'B/S' of the headline, which is an unwanted collision. Its buttons also lost their pill shape and are square-cornered and misaligned (NEW is centred, Try It is offset right), and the bottle floats small in the top-left. B keeps the bottle badge and the pill buttons intact, and the headline is left-aligned and readable. However, everything in B is crammed into the top 60% with a dead empty bottom 40%, the buttons are right-aligned against a left-aligned headline, and the decorative circle is clipped at the top-left corner.

A shrinks everything into the leaderboard. The logo, 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS', the headline, the subcopy, the date, the pills, the RSVP button and the URL line all become microscopic. 'Sunset Sessions' is barely bigger than the body text, so there is no hierarchy. It does keep the CTA and the left-to-right order. B makes 'Sunset Sessions' and 'Saturday 21 June' readable and clearly dominant, but it drops the RSVP button and the logo. Its description paragraph is unreadably small, and 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' sits below the headline instead of above it. The pills are jammed against the top edge.

A is a shrunk copy. The quote is squeezed onto one line at about 7px, so it can't be read in a 320x50 banner. The quote mark is a speck, the product is cut off at the right edge, the SOLSTICE logo is gone, and there is dead space below the text. B is more readable: the quote wraps onto two lines and the yellow quote mark is kept. Its flaws are that the bold yellow attribution is as heavy as the headline, so they compete. The attribution sits left-aligned in a different column from the centered quote. The product is reduced to a thin sliver jammed against the right edge, and the logo is missing.

A is broken. The blurred background photo has come loose from the product and sits as an empty brown box in the middle. The coffee bag sits under it and is cut off at the bottom edge. The body copy is tiny, wraps to leave 'like.' alone on its own line and runs against the margins. The logo and the SAVE badge float off-axis at the top. B has a clear hierarchy, with a strong headline and a sensible top-to-bottom reading order, but it still has problems: the SAVE badge is too big, and the large Q logo circle competes with the product, which has shrunk to a small thumbnail. The CTA is undersized and sits close to the bottom edge.

In A, the headline's 'on' and 'marathons' run into the lime circle, so white text sits on a light lime fill with poor contrast. The shoe is also pulled down and away from its circle, which breaks the original's grouping of shoe and circle, and the NEW VIDEO badge floats with no anchor. B has no collisions, a dominant headline and the shoe kept inside its circle, but the hero image is shrunk into the lower-left corner, 'Full review inside.' sits alone off to the right, and the bottom strip is empty dead space.

A reads left to right and makes the headline dominant, but white 'Full review inside.' sits on the lime circle with poor contrast. The NEW VIDEO badge is cramped and tiny under the logo, and the shoe is shrunk to a speck. B is broken: the shoe is pulled out of its lime circle, which now floats as an empty disc. The logo is too small to read, there is a big dead gap in the middle, and the NEW VIDEO badge is cut off at the right edge.

A keeps every element inside a properly widened card and the headline is clearly dominant. However, the Inkwell & Lantern logo has shrunk to an illegible speck in the top-left corner, which badly weakens the brand. The bottom row (body copy, CTA, fine print) is also crowded, and the tiny legal line sits right beside the button and competes with it. B's card is too narrow for its content: 'The Reading Marathon' and the one-line body copy run past both card edges onto the busy confetti, and the lantern icon pokes out above the card. That breaks the rule against text on a busy background and looks like a mistake, even though B keeps the logo at its proper size.

A reflows the design into a left-to-right banner, and the headline and orange CTA are legible. But the plan cards are out of sequence (6, 80, 48 instead of monthly, yearly, family), the card labels, subtitle and fine print are illegibly small, and the left cluster is cramped. B just shrinks the original portrait layout into the middle of the banner and leaves large empty areas on both sides. All of B's text, including the headline, prices and CTA, is unreadable, so B is unusable.

A stacks everything into the top ~85%, so the subcopy and button are cramped under a headline that breaks onto a second line with 'fizz' left on its own, and a dead band sits at the bottom. It also moves the yellow circle to the top-left, crowding the logo between two shapes and losing the original's opposite-corner balance. B keeps the headline on one line, spaces the elements more evenly down the canvas and keeps the circles in opposite corners. However, B's yellow circle runs behind the subcopy and button, the subcopy breaks awkwardly at 'sparkling / and lightly sweet', and the button has lost its pill shape and become a rounded rectangle, which is off-brand.

A has a sensible left-to-right flow (logo → product → headline → readable CTA pill), but the headline 'Garden-fresh fizz' is shrunk to tiny caption size under a minuscule product, so the CTA and the widely spaced logo outrank the message. B has a large, dominant headline, but the 'Find a Store' CTA is squeezed into an illegible micro-button stacked under the logo against the left edge. The logo, CTA and tiny product are crammed into the left third, so the CTA is effectively lost.

A gets the hierarchy badly wrong. The body copy is set larger than almost everything else, the 'Reserve a Case' CTA is a tiny pill crammed into a right-hand column with 'Ships late June' and the legal text, the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow is gone, and the two-column split at the bottom looks arbitrary. B keeps the original top-to-bottom order with a prominent CTA button and the eyebrow, rule and body text intact, but it has real flaws: the dark header band doesn't reach the canvas edges and the logo is tiny, the headline is small and tightly packed, and the legal line is too small to read.

A keeps the original's centred stack and hierarchy, and nothing collides. Its flaws: the headline wraps to an orphaned 'last', the logo and legal line are very small, and the product sits in a lot of empty space, so it reads as a shrunk portrait layout rather than one rebuilt for a square. B has fragmented hierarchy and grouping. The 'Longest Day Sale' banner is shrunk and stranded at mid-left beside a semi-transparent circle. The logo floats on its own. The subcopy is jammed into a narrow column left of the CTA. The legal text sits on top of the large maroon circle at bottom right. Every element is scattered with no shared grid.

A shrinks everything into a tiny centered text column: the headline is weak, the body copy is illegibly small, the badges are flung to opposite ends of the column, alignment switches between left-aligned GLACIER and centered text, and large dead areas remain. B has a strong headline and a clear left-to-right flow with a dominant CTA, but it's cramped: the circle and the body copy almost touch the canvas edges, the badges nearly collide, GLACIER floats off-axis, and the CTA presses against the bottom edge.

A is the original layout spread out vertically: the logo, headline, body, badges and CTA are separated by huge, uneven gaps, so the group falls apart, and the CTA sits stranded near the bottom with dead space around everything. B groups the copy, badges and CTA into one readable block with strong headline and CTA hierarchy. Its alignment is arbitrary, though: the GLACIER logo, headline, badges and CTA each start at a different left edge. The product circle is pushed into the top-left, leaving the top-right empty, so B is lopsided and still needs fixes.

A: the body copy sits on top of the teal circle, jammed against the left edge. The can is pulled away from its circle backdrop, the GLACIER wordmark now sits below the headline, and the CTA is crammed in with the badges as if it were a peer. Even so, the headline is still clearly the main focal point. B: GLACIER is printed across the circle, and the can is likewise separated from its circle. The headline is shrunk to body size and wraps with 'back' left alone on the second line, which kills the hierarchy. The badges float stranded at the bottom, and the layout is scattered, although the CTA sits cleanly on the right.

A shrinks the green circle into a small blob stuck behind the phone's lower-left corner. The headline runs almost edge to edge, the two badges are staggered on different left edges, and SUMMER ONLY nearly touches the right edge and crowds the CTA. All the text is jammed together while the bottom ~20% of the canvas is empty. B keeps the circle and phone intact, with a clear top-to-bottom flow from brand to headline to product to CTA. Its flaws: the badges now sit below the CTA, there is a big gap between the headline and the phone, alignment switches from a left-aligned headline to centred badges, and the sub-copy is tiny.

A keeps the original's centred stack and a clear headline > subhead > CTA order. Its flaws: the subhead wraps and leaves 'four flavours.' as a short orphan line, the CTA has lost its pill shape and is oversized, and the subhead, button and bottom margin are jammed together while there is extra room at the top. B breaks the single central axis by putting a ragged, centred three-line subhead beside the CTA in an off-centre bottom row, so the lower half looks arbitrary and the subhead gets squeezed small, although the pill button survives.

A: the headline is fairly small for a 320x50 banner, and the CTA pill is tiny. Its 'See the Flavours' label is too small to read, so the CTA gets lost and there's a dead gap between the headline and the button. B: the headline is bigger and fills the height, and the CTA is larger and readable, so it reads left to right in good order. Its flaws: the headline sits tight against the top and bottom edges, and the CTA hugs the right edge with uneven margins.

The two candidates are nearly identical, and both make the same move: they pull the decorative circles fully into the canvas, so the yellow circle now sits as a big disc behind the whole text block and the peach circle frames the CTA. This loses the original's cropped-corner accents and makes the right side feel lopsided. In both, the chip labels are tiny, around 6–7px, and hard to read. A spaces the SOLSTICE wordmark, headline, subline and chips slightly more evenly, while B pushes the wordmark tighter to the headline, so I give A a marginal edge.

Neither is ready to ship. A keeps the original pill shapes, but its left edges don't line up: SOLSTICE starts at about x110, the headline at about x88 and the pills at about x105–108. The CTA floats off to the right with no shared edge, Honey Rosemary is orphaned in the bottom-left, and the large yellow circles sit busily behind the headline. B has a cleaner shared left edge (about x47) for the brand name, headline and subhead, but its pills and button no longer match the original. The button has become a squarer rounded rectangle and the pills have lost their rounded ends. The pill row doesn't line up with the text margin and Honey Rosemary is centred under the other two, and the pink circle runs under the Cucumber Mint pill. Both leave a large empty area to the left of the CTA.

A puts the SOLSTICE wordmark below the headline, so the reading order is broken. Its flavour chips are reversed and jammed against each other, and the body copy is squeezed into a tiny two-line fragment beside them. The oversized CTA is pushed against the right edge while the decorative circles leave dead space on the left. B keeps a sensible order (brand, headline, then copy, CTA and evenly spaced chips in the original sequence), but the headline is jammed against the left and bottom edges and the right cluster feels detached from it.

A keeps the reading order (brand, headline, copy, CTA), but the headline and SOLSTICE sit right against the left edge. The flavour pills are too small to read, and the legal line runs into the peach circle, so both are illegible. B breaks the hierarchy: the CTA comes first at the left edge, SOLSTICE sits under the headline, the pills are reordered, and the subcopy is crammed beside the pills with a 'long season.' widow.

A squeezes all the content into a cramped middle band, leaving a large dead area above and a huge empty gap before the legal text. Its headline is too small to lead, the CTA is pushed right and doesn't line up with the left-aligned text, and the three pills are on inconsistent left edges (Honey Rosemary is offset), so the layout looks random. B uses the tall format properly, with a large headline that clearly leads and a full-width CTA. Its flaws: an oversized gap between the headline and the subcopy, the flavour order reversed from the original (Honey Rosemary now first), centred pills of different widths that don't match the left-aligned text, and the wordmark sitting on the decorative circle.

A: The 'Sunset Sessions' headline is strong, but the RSVP button sits in a 2x2 grid with the badges at the same size, which buries the CTA. The subhead floats above the date and away from the headline. 'Sessions' and the pills crowd the bottom edge, the legal text is tiny and jammed in, and a 'missing asset' placeholder is visible. B: The left brand/headline/subhead block reads in the right order, and the RSVP CTA stands out clearly on the right. However, the TASTINGS pill is cut off from the other two badges, the bottle floats in the middle without purpose, the 'missing asset' box is clipped at the right edge, and the rest of the layout is scattered with uneven empty space. B wins narrowly.

A reads left to right properly: brand and headline, then details and pills, then the RSVP button with its URL. Its flaws are a small headline, a cramped logo/eyebrow block, small tiny-text rows, an orphaned can and a placeholder box pinned to the bottom-right edge. B's reading order is jumbled: the time sits under the logo at far left, the 'Solstice presents' eyebrow is unreadably small, and the URL floats above the subtitle at the right. RSVP is shrunk to a pill the same size as the tags, so the CTA is buried. The pills touch with no gutters, and the placeholder box collides with 'Tastings'.

A: the SOLSTICE logo floats on its own in the empty middle gap, cut off from every other element. The attribution is pushed against the bottom edge, and the can hangs off-centre over a circle that is cropped at the bottom corner. B: the quote, quotation mark and attribution form one tidy column, and the can sits centred in its circle, so the layout reads left to right. Its flaws: the logo is tiny and crammed into the bottom-left, it does not line up with the 108px text column, and the circle is clipped at the top and bottom.

A is a near-uniform shrink of the original. The attribution 'THE GROVE TASTING TEAM' and the SOLSTICE can label are too small to read at this size, and there is a lot of empty space at mid-left. It does keep the original line break, the tracking and the can's sun detail. B has the same shrunk layout and the same unreadable can label. Its attribution has very wide, over-spaced letters that drift from the original typography, and the can is smaller, with its sun motif barely visible. The rewrap of the quote is fine but gains little.

A: the elements use three different left edges. The quote mark sits at about x55, the quote text at about x27 and the attribution is indented at about x50. The attribution is jammed under the last line of the quote and runs into the top edge of the circle. The logo sits inside the circle, which muddies the layering. B: the quote mark, quote text, attribution and logo all share one clean left edge, and the can and circle keep their bottom-right placement from the original. However, 'soon.' is left as a one-word last line, the logo is crammed right under the attribution with no breathing room, and there is a large empty band in the middle left.

A: the quote and attribution are pushed down to the bottom-left with almost no bottom margin, the quote mark is cut off from them at the top, the tiny SOLSTICE logo floats in the empty middle, and the can almost touches the top edge.
